cuda_source = """
#include <torch/extension.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

__global__ void batched_matmul_kernel(const float* A, const float* B, float* C, int batch_size, int m, int k, int n) {
    // Each block handles one (batch, i) pair? Actually we can have grid of blocks per batch.
    // Simpler: each thread computes one output element C[b, i, j].
    // But that's too many threads. We'll do a naive approach:
    int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (idx < batch_size * m * n) {
        int b = idx / (m * n);
        int rem = idx % (m * n);
        int i = rem / n;
        int j = rem % n;
        float sum = 0.0f;
        for (int p = 0; p < k; ++p) {
            // A[b, i, p] and B[b, p, j]
            sum += A[idx * m * k + b * m * k + i * k + p] * B[idx * k * n + b * k * n + p * n + j];
        }
        C[idx] = sum;
    }
}

torch::Tensor batched_matmul_cuda(torch::Tensor A, torch::Tensor B) {
    auto batch_size = A.size(0);
    int m = A.size(1);
    int k = A.size(2); // but A is (batch, m, k)
    int n = B.size(2); // B is (batch, k, n)

    float* A_ptr = A.data_ptr<float>();
    float* B_ptr = B.data_ptr<float>();
    float* C_ptr = torch::zeros_like(A);

    const int block_size = 256;
    const int num_blocks = (batch_size * m * n + block_size - 1) / block_size;

    batched_matmul_kernel<<<num_blocks, block_size>>>(A_ptr, B_ptr, C_ptr, batch_size, m, k, n);

    return C;
}
